Subject: Recap: Technical deep-dive (latency/throughput SLOs & deployment topology)

Alex - thanks again for the deep-dive today. Quick recap and next steps so we all stay aligned.

Key pain points you raised:
- P95 latency target of <= 300ms for short-form generation (max prompt + 256 tokens).
- Sustained throughput of ~120 QPS with bursts up to 350 QPS during business hours.
- Strict data isolation and auditability for production inference; SOC2 + additional logging required.
- Concern about cold-start latency for large models and tail latency during traffic spikes.

What we heard as goals:
- Meet p50/p95 latency targets while keeping unit cost reasonable (target: < $0.003 per 1k tokens).
- Provide predictable capacity with an autoscaling policy that avoids noisy-neighbor interference.
- Ability to run model variants (quantized 70B + 13B fallback) with automated routing based on load and SLOs.

Technical notes / proposed topology (summary):
- Recommended baseline: Dedicated pool (g4dn/g5 equivalent) with VPC Private control plane.
- Model variants: 70B quantized int8 for best quality; 13B int4 as warm fallback for very high throughput windows.
- Serving optimizations: continuous batching with adaptive batch windows, prefix KV caching for prompt re-use, and warm replica pool to reduce cold-start.
- Routing: policy-based routing by latency SLO (route to 70B if estimated latency < 250ms; else 13B).
- Observability: token-level latency/cost breakdown, per-request trace id, and audit log retention (30 days by default; can extend).

Attachments included: redwood-td-deck.pdf (slides), benchmark-template.xlsx (request distribution + sample payloads), redwood-topology-diagram.png.

Open questions / action items:
1) Alex / SRE: share representative request distribution (qps by minute, typical prompt length, and 95/99 percentile tokens) - action: ACME to upload to the Drive folder.
2) Redwood (Dev): run an initial benchmark with your distribution and return RPS/latency curves and cost estimates - action: Dev to run by 2027-06-30.
3) Contract/ops: confirm whether a Dedicated reserved capacity or Private deployment is required for procurement - action: Alex to advise by next week.
4) Follow-up: schedule an SRE-to-SRE sync for topology walkthrough and TLS/KMS details.

Next week I’ll share the benchmark plan and an initial topology diagram for your SREs to comment on. If anything above is off, flag it and I’ll update.

Looping in a slightly more technical runbook based on today’s discussion so the SREs have a concrete starting point. Pasting the short version here; I’ll drop the topology PNG and a benchmark plan into the Drive folder.

Summary topology and benchmark plan:
- Dedicated pool: 8 warm replicas running quantized 70B on A100/RTX-class (or equivalent) with auto-scale group for burst capacity. Warm pool target: 3 replicas reserved to keep KV/cache warm.
- Fallbacks: 4x 13B quantized instances in the same pool that can take routed traffic when estimated 70B latency would exceed SLOs.
- Traffic shaping: adaptive batching with max batch latency 20ms and dynamic batch size based on current QPS; continuous KV caching keyed by conversation_id.
- Cold starts: pre-warm using a short probe traffic generator during scale-up to populate KV cache; use a small pool of instant-start fast-start instances for very short windows.
- Monitoring: per-instance p50/p95/p99, token-level cost inference, and per-route SLA metrics. Alerts on p95 > 300ms or error-rate > 0.5%.

Benchmark steps (Dev -> ACME):
1) Redwood to run 3 benchmarks: baseline (no cache), cached warm (KV hits ~30%), and peak burst (350 QPS) with 60s sustained windows.
2) Each run: measure p50/p95/p99 latency, token/sec, GPU util, and cost per 1k tokens.
3) Deliverable: results CSV + plots and suggested config tweaks. ETA: initial results by 2027-06-30 EOD.

Notes on security/ops:
- We’ll provide SOC2 evidence bundle and recommend KMS integration for any Private deployment.
- Audit logs will be available via S3 export (or customer-managed storage for Private).

If this looks right, I’ll schedule the SRE sync and kick off the benchmark once ACME uploads the sample distribution.
